item.title: Stephen A. Smith hits out at Donald Trump for ‘vengeance tour’ after 2020 presidential election loss
item.description: Credit: Jason Mendez for SiriusXM/Anna Moneymaker via Getty Images Stephen A. Smith acknowledges ‘petty’ claim about how Donald Trump has behaved since coming back to power as the President of the United States. After spending four years out of power following his big loss in 2020, Donald Trump returned for his second term as President of the United States in 2024. Things were going swimmingly for the Republican leader, but all that changed during the 2026 midterm elections. The Democrats enjoyed an incredible evening of results, winning a majority in the House as well as the Senate. Many analysts have suggested that Trump’s decisions and antics are behind this sweeping loss for his party. Stephen A. Smith, who has often straddled the line between right and left, also acknowledged what the POTUS got wrong. Stephen A. Smith agrees Donald Trump went on a ‘vengeance tour’ but also asks Democrats to take responsibility One undeniable fact about the American social and political fabric in recent years has been the obvious divide between people and their beliefs. Those on the right and those on the left have consistently moved further apart, and it has been a breeding ground for a lot of conflict and hatred. Trump has fanned those flames when it has been convenient for him. Stephen A. Smith tried giving a more bipartisan view on it while still acknowledging the president’s role. “You talked about America and how we don’t want the divide, we don’t want the chaos,” Smith said to former DNC Chairman Terry McAuliffe. “You talk as if the Democrats had absolutely nothing to do with that. When you talk about his (Donald Trump’s) vengeance tour, I completely agree. “It’s petty, it’s excessive, it’s unnecessary. Totally true. Forgive the obvious, but what did the Democratic Party think was going to happen when you went after this man after he left office in 2020? His attitude is, ‘I wasn’t doing anything that the other politicians haven’t been doing all these years. I was just better at it. And these people tried to throw me in jail for the rest of my life.’ “How come we couldn’t come up with some way to say, ‘We’ll leave you alone, just get out of the way, don’t ever run for office again.’ How come we couldn’t do that? Why not?” Smith’s takes so far have been quite down the middle politically. While he has suggested he would run for office as a Democrat, he seems to agree with the Republicans on plenty of matters, too. The NBA analyst truly has a lot going on at the moment. item.title: Rutgers wrestling coach opening 20th season with 'most depth I've ever had'
item.description: PISCATAWAY - There is no doubt this is the most highly-anticipated season for the Rutgers University wrestling team since Nick Suriano and current associate head coach Anthony Ashnault became the program's only national champions in 2019. A major part of the excitement is the presence of freshman 125-pounder and former St. John Vianney High School standout Anthony Knox. He is one of five wrestlers to win four NJSIAA championships on the mat. "We think we can win,'' Knox said at the team's Media Day Oct. 29. "This team is good. Guys like me, Barbosa (junior 165-pounder Andrew Barbosa), Remy (senior 197-pounder Remy Cotton), we're gunning for national titles. People might think it's crazy right now, but they're going to see when we start knocking guys off. Then, it becomes real. It's about keeping your mind in the right place. It's a long season.'' More: Anthony Knox era set to begin for Rutgers wrestling: 'I'm here to win' Rutgers, which opens its season Saturday at Journeymen WrangleMania in Bethlehem, Pa. against Long Island University and Navy at 2 and 4 p.m., will have at least seven new starters, including Knox, in its lineup from a year ago. Five NCAA Tournament qualifers from last year graduated and another transferred. Scott Goodale, who begins his 20th season as the Scarlet Knights ' head coach, is excited about the potential this team has. "I think it's the team with the most depth that I've ever had,'' Goodale said at Media Day. "What I mean by that is if somebody we're to get hurt, we have a No. 2 and a No. 3 right behind them that are very, very capable. We are deep at a lot of weights. If somebody asks me to put down our lineup, and I get asked that every day, I can't give them our lineup right now. We're that deep.'' item.title: Stroudsburg quarterback Jackson Mitchell nears new milestone in second 1,000-yard season
item.description: STROUDSBURG – Jackson Mitchell could’ve never thrown another pass after his junior year, and he, statistically, would’ve been one of the best quarterbacks in Stroudsburg football history. The senior signal-caller eclipsed 1,000 passing yards for the first time in 2025, finishing the year with 1,567 yards, breaking the previous single-season record held by recent Stroudsburg and District 11 Hall-of-Fame inductee Jake Jakobsen. In 2026, Mitchell made more history as only the fourth Mountie quarterback to throw for 1,000 yards in back-to-back seasons, joining Jakobsen (2014, 2015), Mike Nikorak (2012, 2013) and Al McCormick (1970, 1971). He ended the regular season with 1,962 passing yards. And if that wasn’t impressive enough, he only needs 38 more yards to be the first 2,000-yard passer in Stroudsburg history. Only eight other quarterbacks accomplished the feat in Pocono area history, and it would only be the 10 th such season if Mitchell joined them (East Stroudsburg South’s Rob Moyer did it twice). ESU Football is inside the Top 20: East Stroudsburg University football cracks coaches poll top 20 for first time since 2006 How did he do it? He turned early experience into consistency. Mitchell split starting quarterback duties as a freshman and sophomore with Ben Pilcher, so when it was time for him to be the full-time starter as a junior, the responsibilities, the atmosphere, and even the players were familiar. Soon, managing the difficulties of the Friday night lights became routine and comfortable, and Mitchell played like it. “Jack being a four-year starter really helps out because he understands what it takes on a game-by-game basis,” head coach Jim Miller said. “He knows what his reads have to be, what he's able to do, and he's got a lot of confidence in all his receivers. “Having him as that dynamic quarterback where he's able to go back there and throw the with confidence in himself and confidence in offensive line really does help out.” Mitchell recalled starting his freshman year, which included the Battle for the Little Brown Jug against a hot East Stroudsburg South squad that went undefeated that October. He admitted he was nervous playing against guys four years older than him at the time, but those moments, along with many others, became lessons. “At this point I've seen everything,” Mitchell said. “I've been on both sides of a blowout; overtimes we’ve won; overtimes we’ve lost. I think all the experiences definitely helped me prepare every week.” When asked specifically about the milestones, Mitchell said that’s something he looks at after the season has concluded. In season, he’s working on a week-to-week basis working to win games, which he and the Mounties are trying to do Nov. 6 in the District 11 6A quarterfinals vs. Whitehall and keep their season going. item.description: Raul Pereda, who is scrambling to regain the PGA Tour card he earned at the 2023 Q School, advanced to second-stage qualifying with a tie for ninth Oct. 27-30 at the Sand Creek Station Golf Club in Newtown, Kan. Pereda, a native of Mexico who has lived in Jacksonville since he was 14 and then played for the Jacksonville University Dolphins, shot 67 in the first round and easily cleared the number to advance with an 11-under 277. The top-18 players, plus ties who shot 6-under or lower, will play in one of five second-stage qualifiers Dec. 1-4. The next step after that is the PGA Tour Q School , presented by Korn Ferry, Dec. 10-13 at the TPC Sawgrass Dye's Valley and the Sawgrass Country Club. Two other Jacksonville residents, former Ohio State golfer Jackson Chandler and former Elon golfer Matthew Doyle, also qualified for second stage. Chandler tied for sixth at The Preserve at Iron Horse in West Palm Beach at 13-under 275, with closing rounds of 66-68, and Doyle tied for 11th at the Abilene (Texas) Country Club at 13-under 275, with a 66 in the final round. Other area residents who previously advanced from first-stage qualifying are former University of North Florida players Brandon Mancheno and Robbie Higgins, former Florida Gator Tyson Alexander, Sam Nicholson and Carl Yuan. item.title: Can FAMU football stop Jaylon Tolbert? Chris Cash's big first test
item.description: Game recognizes game. As a former star college quarterback himself, Florida A&M head football coach Quinn Fordham Gray Sr. is taking notice of what Jaylon Tolbert is doing under center for the Alcorn State Braves . “He’s really just a talented guy that can make plays with his legs and arm,” Gray said of FAMU’s next quarterback matchup coming this Saturday. “So we’ll have our hands full with that.” Tolbert enters the Week 10 Southwestern Athletic Conference clash against the Rattlers as the leading passer in the entire NCAA Division I Football Championship Subdivision. The senior from Fort Lauderdale sits atop the nation with 2,681 passing yards and is tied for first with 27 touchdowns with South Dakota’s Austyn Modrzewski. He’s completed 65% of passes and only thrown eight interceptions in nine games, with four coming in a Football Bowl Subdivision game against Southern Mississippi back in September. The 6-foot-2, 175-pounder has also rushed 71 times for 269 yards and three touchdowns. Tolbert is quite the opening test for safeties and nickelbacks coach Christopher Cash, who enters his first game as the defensive playcaller after Gray made the switch from defensive coordinator and linebackers coach Ryan Lewis Sr. after nine games. The struggling unit is 10th out of 12 in SWAC total defense, with league-worst run defense as the main culprit. The Rattlers’ pass defense is sixth in the conference. The key to FAMU cooling down Tolbert is a “sound” and “simplified” strategy that gives defenders leeway to “play fast.” Led by Tolbert, Alcorn erupted for 585 total offensive yards in a 52-17 win over Mississippi Valley State. The quarterback went 23-for-29 for 320 passing yards, threw three touchdowns, and rushed for one. The Braves have the highest-scoring offense in the FCS, at 43 points per game. “It’s going to take a concerted effort, a collective effort from the coaching staff and then also from the players,” Gray previewed FAMU-Alcorn. “We have to allow our guys to go out there and be confident in what it is that we’re doing and the calls that are being made.” Alcorn State likes to stretch the field and spread the football. item.title: Former F1 champion Jones dies aged 80
item.description: Jones helped turn Williams into one of the major forces in F1 [Getty Images] Alan Jones, the last Australian and first Williams driver to win the Formula 1 world title, has died at the age of 80. Jones raced in F1 between 1975 and 1986, winning the title in 1980 to become the first of Williams' seven world champions. Jones, who turned 80 on Monday, won 12 grands prix in his career and raced competitively in other formats until 2002. "We are extremely saddened to announce the passing of our beloved Alan, who passed away on 5 November following a short illness," his wife Amanda Butler-Davis said in a statement released on her behalf by Motorsport Australia. "He will be dearly missed and fondly remembered by those closest to him, as well as the many fans whose support he was always grateful for." Jones started the first of his 116 F1 races in a Hesketh at the 1975 Spanish Grand Prix. He won his first race for the Shadow team in Austria in 1977 before joining Williams the following year. After finishing third in the drivers' championship in 1979, he won five races in 1980 and finished on the podium in all but one of the grands prix he completed, taking the title ahead of Nelson Piquet. Jones was the second Australian to win the F1 championship, after Jack Brabham in 1959, 1960 and 1966. Jones remains the most recent Australian to triumph at the Australian Grand Prix, winning at Melbourne's Calder Park Raceway in 1980 when the race was not part of the world championship. He finished third in the drivers' standings in 1981, winning in Las Vegas for what proved to be his final race victory. He retired at the end of the season. Having appeared in one race for Arrows in 1983, Jones made a full-time comeback with new team Haas in 1985 and raced largely unsuccessfully the following year. He continued to compete in touring car and endurance races, mostly in Australia, and became a popular motorsports pundit on television in his home country. "Alan dedicated his life to motorsport, building a legacy that will live on through the countless people he touched along the way," Butler-Davis said. "Through his achievements, passion and unmistakable character, both on and off the track, Alan left an enduring mark on the sport both nationally and across the globe." Breaking new ground with Williams Jones, the Williams FW07 and Patrick Head and Frank Williams in Brazil in 1981 [Getty Images] Alan Jones' time at the very peak of F1 was short - essentially just under three years from mid-1979 to the end of 1981 - but he left a lasting impression. Jones is synonymous with the Williams team, having become their first world champion in 1980, and he formed a close, almost brotherly bond with co-founders Frank Williams and Patrick Head. Williams and Head loved Jones' pugnacious, no-nonsense approach, and between them they were the leading force in F1 for a short time, as the team first emerged at the forefront of the sport. item.title: How Sammy Brown keeps playing like star LB amid Clemson football's roller-coaster seasons
item.description: CLEMSON — Clemson football has changed over the past three years. Sammy Brown hasn't. As the Tigers have navigated turbulence, underwhelming seasons and disappointing losses, the junior linebacker has remained the same relentlessly consistent player that he was when he arrived as one of the nation's top recruits. Brown racked up a team-high 106 tackles last season and has 51 tackles with two sacks this season for Clemson (5-3, 3-2 ACC) heading into its game at Syracuse (4-4, 2-4) on Nov. 7 (noon, ESPN2). Brown was the ACC Defensive Rookie of the Year in 2024, a first-team All-ACC selection in 2025 and now a Butkus Award semifinalist in 2026. Brown's career has gone according to plan. Almost too much so. "It's like you try to convince yourself that there's got to be something," said Travis Noland, Brown's coach at Jefferson High School in Georgia. "There's got to be some weakness, there's got to be some flaw, and there's just not." Brown hasn't had an expectation he hasn't met. In fact, he’s exceeded several of them. There hasn’t seemed to have been a bar that Brown hasn’t cleared. High school evaluators expected him to be a stud. Clemson's coaches expected him to be one of their best. Now, Brown is projected to play in the NFL as a first- or second-round pick. So far, nobody's been wrong yet. "Nobody has to question or wonder if Sammy's going to show up and play. He always does," Noland said. "There are a lot of people who can bring it when they feel good, but Sammy does it every day." How Sammy Brown earned his reputation Brown began clearing lofty expectations long before he arrived at Clemson. Eastern Michigan linebacker Kadin Bailey, Brown's teammate at Jefferson High, remembers his first game in 2021. Brown lined up at running back and took his first carry 78 yards for a touchdown, then showed off his physicality at linebacker to help Jefferson defeat Rabun County 22-13. Brown only went up from there, winning MaxPreps Male National Athlete of the Year, USA TODAY National Defensive Football Player of the Year and the High School Butkus Award, among many other accolades. "There was nothing Sammy couldn't do," Bailey said. "He could have gone to college as a running back. We even played him at quarterback for a couple of games." What separated Brown was that he never acted like a five-star recruit. His approach remained the same, regardless of what he did. "It's easy, once you get labeled a five-star, to sit back and think everything's just gonna be handed to you," Bailey said. "But he didn't. He just kept working and got better every day." item.title: One year after 'Let it Rip' meeting, Trevor Lawrence has elevated game
item.description: The Jacksonville Jaguars were a surprising 4-3, but his quarterback was still searching to sync his in-week preparation and game-day production when Liam Coen welcomed Trevor Lawrence into his second-floor office on Oct. 20, 2025. Lawrence was a tireless worker who made the right pre-snap decisions but was plagued by bouts of indecisiveness. Before sending him on his bye week, Coen showed Lawrence multiple examples in which the play was right there had he pulled the trigger. “I just have to trust it,” Lawrence told Coen. The summit could eventually be remembered as one of the most important meetings — The "Let It Rip" meeting — in Jaguars history. The coach showed confidence and belief in his franchise quarterback but also urged him to be more aggressive. In the 17 regular season games since, the Jaguars are 14-3 and Lawrence has totals of 37 touchdowns, 11 interceptions, 4,669 passing yards, a 63.9 completion rate and a 109.9 passer rating. High-level stuff. MVP stuff. Winning stuff. A player who used to tease with bits of elite play is now one of the NFL’s best quarterbacks. He enters the Jaguars’ Nov. 5 game at the Baltimore Ravens with a league-best 112.6 passer rating; he started the season with a career 86.3 rating. The Jaguars are 5-2 thanks in part to Lawrence’s level-jump — check that, multi-level jump. Just as the Chicago Bears have been reborn with the Ben Johnson and Caleb Williams, so have the Jaguars with Coen and Lawrence. Admit it: For the first time since maybe 1999, you, the Jaguars fan, expects your team to win every week and when they don’t, there is a sky-is-falling reaction. Feels good, doesn’t it? It sure does within Jaguars headquarters, where the collaboration between Coen and Lawrence has advanced to the pro football equivalent of Ph.D. courses. “Very far,” Coen told The Times-Union on Oct. 20 of Lawrence's progress. “I’m very, very pleased with how he’s seeing things.” What is it like to be around Coen and Lawrence in the quarterback meeting room, when class is in session and plays are tossed out, added or revised? item.title: Today in Boston Celtics history: Cs' 1st home game; Walton born; Radja, Rivas, Loscy debut; Englund passes
item.description: Today in Boston Celtics history, The Boston Celtics, a newly-formed professional basketball franchise, played their first home game in 1946 in the Basketball Association of America (BAA), a precursor to the NBA. The game resulted in a narrow loss, 57-55, to the now-defunct Chicago Stags (not to be confused with the later Chicago Bulls ). Two Celtics players scored in double figures, including guard Johnny Simmons, who contributed 13 points from 6 field goals and a free throw. However, much of what else went on in that game remains unknown, as many statistics were not recorded during this early era of the sport. Wyndol Gray scored 12 points as well, and future star of television and film Chuck Connors added 8 points in the loss. Historic milestones Dino Radja played his first game for Boston on this date in 1993 in a 111-108 loss to the New York Knicks in which Radja scored 15 points, 8 rebounds, 3 assists, and a block. It was also big man Acie Earl's first game with the team, in which he logged 15 points to go with his 4 boards and a steal. Ramón Rivas debuted for the team in 1988 in a 129-115 loss to the Philadelphia 76ers on this date as well. Rivas pulled down 3 rebounds while missing both of his field-goal attempts. 33 years to the day earlier, forwards Dick Hemric and Jim Loscutoff played their first minutes for the team in 1955 in a 98-87 win over the (then) Philadelphia (now, Golden State) Warriors. The Wake Forest alum scored 5 points, going 2-for-4 from the floor, while the future seven-time champ Loscy got 3 points and 2 assists. Birthdays It is also former Celtic center Bill Walton's birthday, born today in 1952 in La Mesa, California. A UCLA alum, Walton was taken first overall in the 1974 NBA Draft by the Portland Trail Blazers and would play for that team and the (then) San Diego Clippers (now, Los Angeles) before being dealt to the Celtics for Cedric Maxwell. Walton had engineered the trade himself after reaching out to the Los Angeles Lakers and Boston, with Boston more inclined to take on the risk of his frequent injuries. The UCLA alum won a title with the team that season (and take the team to see the Grateful Dead that fall on his birthday), playing for the Celtics for 90 games spread over two seasons. He averaged 7 points, 6.4 rebounds, and 1.4 assists per game with Boston – rest in peace. Gone too soon Finally, it is also the date of former Celtics center Gene Englund's passing in 1995. An alumnus of the University of Wisconsin, Englund signed with the Celtics as a free agent at the start of the 1949-50 NBA season, who he played 24 games for before being dealt to the (then) Tri-Cities Blackhawks (now, Atlanta Hawks). item.title: Jeremiah Smith is 164 yards from another Big Ten record
item.description: LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 31: Jeremiah Smith #4 of the Ohio State Buckeyes in action against the USC Trojans during the second quarter at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum on October 31, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images) | Getty Images Lost in the frustration of Ohio State’s 30-18 loss at USC was another piece of history from Jeremiah Smith. With just over two minutes left, Luke Fahey found him for a one yard touchdown. It was the 40th touchdown catch of Smith’s career, breaking Braylon Edwards’ Big Ten record of 39, which had stood since 2004. It didn’t feel like much of a celebration in the moment, but it’s worth remembering just how fast Smith is rewriting the record books. Smith already owns every major receiving record at Ohio State, and now he holds the Big Ten’s career touchdown mark too. The next record could fall this Saturday. The yardage record is within reach Smith caught 10 passes for 83 yards at USC, giving him 3,625 career receiving yards. The Big Ten record belongs to Purdue’s John Standeford, who finished with 3,788 yards from 2000 to 2003. That puts Smith 163 yards from tying the record and 164 from breaking it. That’s a big number for most receivers. For Smith, it’s an ordinary afternoon. He had 151 yards against Ball State, 164 at Texas, 217 against Illinois and 206 at Iowa. He’s averaging over 130 receiving yards per game this season, with 62 catches for 1,067 yards and 13 touchdowns through eight games. When I wrote about the Big Ten record chase in early October, I predicted JJ would break this one at USC on Halloween. Sayin’s injury, a quiet day at Indiana and USC’s game plan pushed it back a week. The timing might work out even better. Breaking it at home against Oregon, in front of the Ohio Stadium crowd, would be a pretty fitting way to do it. Can he get there with Fahey? That’s the real question. Smith’s production has dipped over the last two games. Against Indiana, he had a season-low 68 yards against a defense that threw extra bodies at him on almost every snap. At USC, with Fahey making his first start, he caught 10 passes but averaged just 8.3 yards per catch as Ohio State leaned on quick, short throws. That makes sense. Fahey needed easy completions, and Smith is the most reliable target on the field. But it also means the big plays haven’t been there. To get 164 yards against Oregon, Smith will probably need at least one or two explosive plays down the field. I think there’s reason to believe those will come. Fahey now has a full game under his belt and another week of practice as the starter. Smith said after Indiana that it would, “take time” to build the same chemistry with a new quarterback, but he’s already Fahey’s top target. Smith also caught the record breaking touchdown at USC, which tells you Fahey is looking for him when it matters most. The more reps those two get together, the more comfortable Fahey should be giving Smith a chance to make a play down the field.
